title: Signal fusion and automated remediation for VPC healthchecks under token saturation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: During heavy token ingestion we observe intermittent bursts of tail latency and elevated 5xx rates in private (VPC) deployments. Existing synthetic probes surface individual signals (latency, errors, token drop), but there is no unified signal that: 1) correlates across windows, 2) suppresses noisy transient spikes, and 3) triggers safe automated remediation (e.g., autoscale, shed tokens, rollback upgrade). This ticket implements a lightweight 'signal fusion' layer plus Terraform hooks to wire remediation actions into private deployments and upgrade pipelines.
acceptance_criteria: A unified health signal ("fusion_score") computed from latency p95/p99, error-rate (5xx), worker token throughput, and queue saturation that is published to the tenant SLO topic every 30s.
Terraform module change to private/vpc/modules/health must expose two new provisioned resources: synthetic-token-load job and fusion_score_alerting_policy with configurable thresholds.

Automated remediation playbooks wired: (a) autoscale worker pool with cooldown, (b) soft-token-shed via upstream rate-limit config, (c) canary rollback trigger during rolling upgrade. Remediation must be gated by a 3-out-of-5 fusion_score sliding window to avoid flapping.
Unit and integration tests validate fusion_score behavior under synthetic scenarios (bursty tokens, slow kernels, KV-cache thrash).
Dashboards: SLO composer shows fusion_score, contributing signals, and remediation actions with a timeline overlay.
Documentation: Confluence runbook + Terraform usage example and example policy for tenant ops team.
No regressions on existing probe exporters (existing metrics still emitted).
implementation_notes: Add a small sidecar: health-synthesizer (Go) that subscribes to metrics-exporter stream, computes fusion_score using weighted percentiles and EWMA for smoothing.
Weights: default weights (latency_p95: 0.35, latency_p99: 0.15, error_rate_5xx: 0.30, token_throughput_drop: 0.20) configurable per tenant via TF variables.
Expose fusion_score as a gauge: redwood.vpc.fusion_score{tenant,region} and as an event to the SLO topic for downstream pipelines.
Terraform: new module variable 'fusion_alerting' with objects encoded as maps (strings) for thresholds. Provide example: fusion_score > 0.7 for 90s triggers alert.
Integrate with existing autoscaler: add action hook to call Autoscaler API with desired worker delta and reason tag 'fusion_remediation'.
Upgrade pipeline: add step that pauses canary rollout when fusion_score breaches canary threshold and triggers rollback if unresolved after cooling period.
Keep sidecar resource footprint low; default replica set 1 per availability zone. Use circuit-breaker for exporter backpressure to avoid causing additional load.
test_plan: Unit tests for fusion computation (weights, smoothing, sliding windows).
Integration test using synthetic-token-load job to reproduce token pressure and validate remediation path (in CI ephemeral VPC).
Chaos scenario: simulate KV cache miss storm and ensure fusion_score increases and triggers soft token shedding but not immediate rollback for transient spikes.
Load test: validate telemetry load from health-synthesizer scales to supported tenants (benchmarks attached in artifacts).
Manual verification checklist for SRE: dashboard views, alert-to-remediation latency, and policy tuning guidance.
rollout_plan: Alpha: deploy to internal 'staging-private' VPC for 1 week. Run synthetic scenarios and tune weights.
Beta: enable for three low-traffic customers behind feature flag; monitor fusion_score and remediation frequency for 2 weeks.
GA: opt-in Terraform variable default enabled for new private deployments; documented migration path for existing customers.
Emergency rollback: remove health-synthesizer sidecar via TF destroy and disable alerting policy; documented runbook in Confluence.
Post-deploy: 30-day review to tune thresholds based on real workload; feed findings into Optimize recommendations.
risks: Fusion logic may overreact to correlated noise and trigger autoscaling that increases cost—mitigated by sliding-window voting and cooldowns.
Sidecar publishing may add telemetry load; will rate-limit and sample metrics to avoid overload.
Terraform changes touching customer infra must be opt-in; accidental enablement could change behavior—use explicit variable with default=false.
Misconfigured weights may hide important signals (e.g., underweighting token drop). Provide sane defaults and quick tuning knobs.
